fact: The High Constitutional Court's decision of 27 January 2017 declares Law 2016-056 of 16 December 2016 on electronic money and e-money institutions, adopted by both chambers on 14 and 16 December 2016, in conformity with the Constitution before promulgation; it states Madagascar's positive law held no e-money provisions until then.

fact: The decision states that under Law 2016-056 all e-money operations must go through an e-money institution licensed by the CSBF (banking and financial supervision commission), the regulator of those institutions, with disciplinary and penal sanctions for breach.
system: Loi n°2016-056 sur la monnaie électronique et les établissements de monnaie électronique

fact: 2424.mg reports that the law on e-money institutions (EME) is applied by the CSBF, which under it issues regulatory instructions, grants or withdraws licences and audits EMEs; the BFM governor announced audits of EMEs on 2026-06-11 after user complaints.

fact: 2424.mg reports that under the EME law the CSBF grants and withdraws licences of e-money institutions, which are audited and held to consumer-protection duties such as a 24/7 customer service; the article names no institution.
system: Loi sur les établissements de monnaie électronique

fact: Loi n°2016-056 on electronic money and electronic money institutions, adopted by the National Assembly and Senate on 14 and 16 December 2016 and cleared by the High Constitutional Court on 27 January 2017, was promulgated on 2 February 2017 and is to be published and executed as state law.
system: Loi n°2016-056 sur la monnaie électronique et les établissements de monnaie électronique

fact: Loi n°2016-056 (2017) requires any legal entity running e-money operations to be approved by the CSBF as an e-money institution (a limited company, articles 11, 24 and 33), separate from credit institutions and microfinance institutions, which may also run e-money with CSBF authorisation (articles 34 and 36).

fact: A Banky foiben'i Madagasikara instruction of October 2024 obliges CSBF-licensed banks and e-money institutions, and large microfinance institutions, to connect to its instant payment system (SPI), with deadlines of 31 January 2025 for banks and e-money institutions.
Banking law 2020-011 governs e-money institutions, giving the CSBF power to regulate and control them, inspect their distribution agents and withdraw licences.
